_comment: Why: Firefox can resolve DNS itself over HTTPS, bypassing the OS resolver
entirely. When it does, Pi-hole never sees the query -- no blocklists, no
query log, no per-client visibility. Every other layer in the DNS chain
(DNS Director, Pi-hole, the router's DoT) is irrelevant to a browser doing
Pi-hole already returns NXDOMAIN for use-application-dns.net, Mozilla's
canary domain, which disables DoH network-wide for every Firefox on the
LAN. That is the right first layer, but it is only honoured while
network.trr.mode is at its default. Ticking 'Enable DNS over HTTPS' in
Settings overrides the canary and the bypass returns silently.
Locked: true greys the setting out so it cannot be re-enabled per-profile,
and unlike a prefs.js edit it survives a profile reset or a new profile.
# restart Firefox, then confirm at about:policies
